chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: The Apollo audience, the theater circuit and nearly becoming mayor of Harlem
summary: The Apollo led to a circuit of Black theaters no other white band played; he calls it his greatest audience, set a house record, and nearly won honorary mayor of Harlem around 1939.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, he used to get these soft mallets and he'd start banging away on these pieces of the xylophone, and they'd fly off into space and, you know, it was -- he had done this act in vaudeville. So he had a little act there that he did, and the band went over real good. Ralph Cooper was the master of ceremonies. Pig Meat Markham was there doing his thing, and [Puerto Rico] on the amateur night, you know, shooting the gun off and coming out in the grass. skirt and grabbing to grab all the people that didn't make it. That was my first -- from then on we -- I must have played the Apollo -- I used to play the piano, oh, four times a year, and it became, you know, a steady and wonderful experience. And through that we were also able to -- we had a chain of theaters that we inherited all the other black theaters around, like the Howard in Washington and the Royal in Baltimore and the Paradise in Detroit and the Regal in Chicago. We had our own little
circuit of theaters that no other white band had.

And it was quite an experience. And I still say that is the greatest audience I have ever played to in my life. Boy, when that curtain came flying up and everybody -- it was an exhilaration, and they used to pour it on you. We did as many as eight shows a day there. We at one time held the house record for business.
At the Apollo. In fact, I don't know if you know this or not, but I came within 200 votes of being elected honorary mayor of Harlem.
Oh, back in the -- around the time of '39 or around the time of, "Cherokee." Billy -- Willy Bryant beat me out by about 214 votes.
Aw. Now, that's an accomplishment. It really is.
Things ain't what they used to be.
